title: Checked before the bike
objective: Check glucose around exercise in patients with diabetes as the plan directs: give fast-acting carbohydrate if it falls below 100 mg/dL, and tell the PT
secondaryObjectives: Recognizing and responding to signs of hypo/hyperglycemia during a treatment session

brief.situation: 11:15 in an outpatient rehabilitation clinic. You are the physical therapist assistant. Mr. Sato, 59, has type 1 diabetes and is on visit 3 of prosthetic gait training. He skipped breakfast to make the appointment and took his usual morning insulin.
handover: Plan of care (Dr. Wu, PT): check glucose before exercise and every 20 minutes; below 100 mg/dL give fast-acting carbohydrate, recheck in 15 minutes, and tell the PT before exercising; stop at any symptoms of low glucose.
The clinic keeps glucose tablets and juice at the front desk.
Dr. Wu is in the clinic.
howItWorks: The clock runs in simulated time at the pace you choose: study pace (3x) or exam realism (1x). Pause any time.
Each question or measure takes the time on its button. Decide what to collect, what it means for today's session and who needs to know.
Partway through you are asked to write your reasoning. A debrief scores what you did.

scoring.modelReasoning: The plan says to check glucose before exercise. After insulin without breakfast it reads in the 80s, below the plan's 100 threshold, and he soon becomes shaky. The PTA holds exercise, gives fast-acting carbohydrate, rechecks in 15 minutes and tells the supervising PT, who adjusts the session; insulin questions go to his prescriber.
